title: Yiwen website redesign v4
text:
Yiwen website redesign v4
This version implements the latest requested edits:

Removes hyperlinks from supervisor names on the homepage.
Adds Forbes China 30 Under 30 (2023) with the official Forbes China link.
Hides Quarto hover anchor icons.
Reorders public work: SheShapes AI, World Economic Forum Global Shapers, Future Youth.
Revises GV101 teaching wording and keeps the LSE course guide link.
Removes the Work in Progress section from the Research page.
Adds links for Forbes and the UN News interview item.
Rephrases Intergenerational Exchange entry to avoid the weak “selected participant” wording.

Replace the corresponding files in your Quarto project root, then run:
quarto preview .
quarto render .
Commit both the source files and the generated docs/ directory.

title: Research
text:
My research sits at the intersection of inequality, comparative political economy, computational social science, and AI governance. I study how welfare institutions, economic insecurity, and technological change shape political behaviour, public opinion, and policy-relevant attitudes.



The Politics of Unequal Protection: Three Essays on Welfare States, Economic Insecurity, and Technological Change
Doctoral research project. This project develops the concept of expected residual loss to explain how institutional protection shapes the translation of economic insecurity into political demand.





Aggregate Agreement Is Not Validity: Three Levels of Evidence for LLM-Simulated Public Opinion in China and Britain
Working paper; presented at APSA 2026. This paper develops claim-dependent validation for synthetic survey respondents and identifies cross-public structural substitution in redistribution attitudes.


Hung, Ho Ting, Nachiket Midha, Victor Y. Wu, and Yiwen Zhang. 2026. “Multi-dimensional Bias in Modeling Multi-dimensional Preferences: Evaluating the Ability of Synthetic Agents to Replace Human Participants in Conjoint Experiments.” Working paper / arXiv preprint.
arXiv





Burland, Patrick, and Yiwen Zhang. 2025. “Seeing beyond the negative: An examination of key variables in the different reasons for the decisions not to formally recognise people as survivors of modern slavery.” Modern Slavery and Human Rights Policy and Evidence Centre, University of Oxford, in collaboration with IOM UK. Policy report.

title: Yiwen Zhang
text:
Yiwen Zhang
    张译文
    PhD Candidate in Political ScienceLSE Government

    
      Download CV
      Email
      LinkedIn
    
    CV updated: September 2026
  

  
    
      About
      Researching inequality, welfare institutions, and technological change.
      
        I am a PhD candidate in the Department of Government at the London School of Economics and Political Science (LSE), affiliated with the Data Science Institute and supervised by Professor Valentino Larcinese and Dr Pavithra Suryanarayan. I am fully funded as a first-cohort Enlighten Scholar.
      
      
        Before joining LSE, I completed my M.Phil. and B.A. in Political Science (with joint honour program in Politics, Law, and Sociology) at Peking University.
      
      
        My research sits at the intersection of inequality, comparative political economy, computational social science, and AI governance. I study how welfare institutions and technological change shape economic insecurity, political demand, public opinion, and policy-relevant attitudes.
      
      
        As a first-generation university student from Sichuan, China, I also work on public initiatives that connect research with education equity, youth leadership, and inclusive technology. I was named to Forbes China 30 Under 30 (2023) in the Social Enterprise category.

title: Outreach
text:
I connect research with public action through inclusive technology, education equity, youth leadership, and cross-sector collaboration.



SheShapes AI
Co-founder. SheShapes AI supports inclusive AI literacy, leadership, and social impact through fellowships, workshops, mentoring, and community-based learning.


Future Youth
Co-founder. An education equity initiative supporting students from under-resourced backgrounds through mentorship, workshops, and public-facing educational resources.





World Economic Forum Global Shapers Community — Beijing Hub
Global Shaper, Beijing Hub Curator, and Youth Pulse Sub-Regional Steward for Greater China and North Asia. I have contributed to youth-led initiatives on gender equality, education equity, technology, and social impact.


Schwab Foundation × Global Shapers Community Intergenerational Exchange
Selected for the 2026 Intergenerational Exchange, a cross-generational dialogue programme connecting emerging and established social innovators.





Forbes China 30 Under 30
Recognised in the Social Enterprise category in 2023.


United Nations News Interview — “青年力量：为可持续发展目标行动”
Interviewed as a youth delegate of the China SDGs Initiative, discussing education equity, gender empowerment, and youth-led action.
